The preparation is followed by a tasting.

The class takes place in a restaurant over an open fire. You will prepare meat on long skewers, along with cheese, garlic rolls, corn, chicken hearts and pineapple with cinnamon.

After cooking, everything can be tasted fresh from the grill. Pineapple with cinnamon is a special part of the barbecue: the heat caramelizes the sugar, and the sweet fruit becomes part of the same feast as the meat and appetizers.

At 9:00, the guide will pick you up from your hotel. The city portion of the route passes through San Antonio Park, San Ignacio Square and La Playa Avenue. You will then visit the Sculpture Park, with more than 20 works donated by Fernando Botero, the Park of Wishes, the Atanasio Girardot sports arena and Pueblito Paisa, a recreation of a traditional Colombian village.

A separate part of the day is devoted to El Poblado. The route includes El Poblado Park, Lleras Park and the Golden Mile, an area concentrating the city's hotels and business activity.

The final part of the excursion focuses on Medellín's historical memory. You will visit neighborhoods and sites connected with the period of Pablo Escobar, San Pedro Cemetery and the Memory Museum. Here the city's history is explored through the lives of people who experienced the violence of those years.

In the morning, you will take a sightseeing tour of the city and Comuna 13, visiting the city's main attractions, including:
San Antonio Park, San Ignacio Square, the traditional La Playa Avenue, Sculpture Park (with more than 20 sculptures donated by the artist Fernando Botero), the Park of Wishes, the Atanasio Girardot sports complex, the renovated La Macarena Convention Center (formerly a bullring) and traditional Pueblito Paisa.
You will then be taken to the El Poblado district, where you will visit El Poblado Park, Lleras Park and the Golden Mile, the city's financial and hotel district.
The excursion continues to Comuna 13 in Medellín, where you will discover graffiti depicting important moments in its history.
These murals were created by various local artists, telling stories that move visitors and inspire hope.

Your introduction to Medellín begins at Botero Square. You will visit the Museum of Antioquia and see the Rafael Uribe Uribe Palace of Culture and the historic Veracruz Church.

Next, you will head to Comuna 13. Its murals, outdoor escalators and lively streets reveal how this neighborhood has changed. It is an excellent place to explore street art and observe everyday city life.

The final stop, El Castillo Museum, transports you to a different setting. The European-style mansion houses works of art, antiques and furniture from different periods, surrounded by well-tended gardens. After the excursion, return to the hotel.
